gates.rationale: The first profile is an exact default-deny manifest and startup admission gate.
Code and weights DGM remain research-only and every production execution/promotion path is refused.
Unfinished clients, runtimes, and optional distributions are omitted and hidden from the first profile.
Every discovered connector has an explicit non-production support tier, and the first profile admits none; catalog counts cannot be represented as live support.
The checked-in external-effect contract defines PREPARED, COMMITTED, REFUSED, and INDETERMINATE semantics and regression checks prohibit universal exactly-once wording.

The repository now has a fail-closed service-objective schema and approval contract, but every target, measurement source, evidence reference, and approval remains intentionally empty. Product, reliability, security, recovery, and support owners must approve measured objectives before this gate can close.

One source policy binds production paths, owners, workflow authority, artifact staging, rollback/provenance checks, and release-state manifests. External branch and environment enforcement remains tracked under DEP-17 and the release gates.
Buyer documents are hash-bound to a conservative claim ledger that distinguishes repository facts, source inventory, draft policy, historical evidence, and deployment/external evidence requirements.
Required Shield composition distinguishes detector failure and blocks.
Real Shield failure paths and required call sites have adverse regressions.
Consequential effects require durable audit preparation and honest completion state.
Finance assessment APIs enforce tenant, suite, record, and action authority.
Proxy SSO identity cannot be bypassed by an invite session.
Sealed child output is withheld before hooks, traces, and callbacks.

The source now requires exactly one production identity provider, recomputes a secret-free provider/RBAC posture digest at every authentication decision and app-wide authorization boundary, default-denies unsupported SAML/shared-token/local-invite modes, binds the posture into signed onboarding evidence, and delivers exact non-secret Helm inputs through an immutable content-addressed ConfigMap while keeping credentials in the Secret projection. The gate remains pending because no exact-release live IdP/proxy, session, SCIM/revocation, role-assignment, break-glass, or end-to-end attribution evidence is recorded; mutable customer rosters also remain live change-controlled evidence rather than source-bound inputs.

The exact endpoint registry, reviewed background-job kinds, production tool registry, and supported operator command set are default-deny and fingerprint/contract checked; MCP, plugins, connectors, and callbacks are excluded.

Plain bus data is structurally non-authoritative; capability changes require signed audience-bound delegation with finite expiry, replay protection, roster checks, and no downgrade on verification failure.
Untrusted bus records retain provenance, are bounded and detached, pass required fail-closed Shield screening, are withheld on detector error, and cannot be reinterpreted as instruction authority.

Admitted audit, hook, exception, durable-job, trace, and support paths quarantine or emit bounded metadata on redaction/classification failure; voice, attachment, connector, channel, and plugin egress are absent from the profile.

Session and invitation code enforces secure cookie posture, origin/CSRF rules, state replay protection, bounded lifetime, logout/revocation, invite single use, role/identity revocation, and exact principal attribution. Live IdP qualification remains SEC-07.
The first profile admits no third-party plugin package, discovery path, runtime overlay, manifest, or tool; preflight and direct-invocation tests refuse plugin enablement before import.
Vendor-console code, connected entitlement polling, root entitlement authority, credentials, routes, and packages are absent from and refused by the customer production artifact.

Dashboard query credentials are rejected before routing, signed-link routes are absent from the production registry and return 404 without token reflection, and deployment guidance uses authorization headers rather than URL credentials.

Sensitive reads and publications use handle-bound custody with ownership/mode checks and refuse ancestor/final symlinks, reparse points, hard links, aliasing, and path-swap/ABA races on supported filesystem seams.

Repository security regressions do not substitute for an independent scoped penetration test against the exact candidate deployment. No external assessor report, remediation record, retest, scope, or expiry is available.
Configured secret custody never falls back to ambient environment authority.
Audit redaction failure cannot persist the original plaintext payload.

Hooks declare explicit privileges and classifications, receive bounded projections, cannot access sealed data, credentials, raw reasoning, or unredacted output by default, and fail with audited semantics.
Arbitrary command/code execution is disabled; no local-host fallback exists in the profile.
A default-deny NetworkPolicy template exists, but no exact-release cluster/CNI egress-denial result or rendered live policy is recorded.

Production startup admits a read-only image/root plus only the exact workspace, state, temporary, configuration, and staged-secret mounts. It refuses host credentials, runtime sockets, control-plane paths, unexpected read-only mounts, aliases, and cross-tenant path custody before serving.

Code and Helm contracts bound CPU, memory, PIDs, open files, single-file and temporary storage, output, tokens, wall time, tool calls, concurrency, and nested agents. The gate remains pending until the exact cluster proves cgroup/storage/network enforcement and whole-process-tree termination under exhaustion.

The production Dockerfile and Helm profile declare an unprivileged user, non-root security context, dropped capabilities, seccomp, and read-only root. No exact image inspection plus target-cluster admission/runtime result proves every shipped production image actually runs non-root.

Every admitted model-visible tool and direct or flow dispatch is classified by a default-deny contract that binds capability, tenant, principal, resources, approval, Shield, sandbox, and required audit policy. Unclassified paths refuse, while MCP, plugins, connectors, callbacks, and consequential tools are excluded from this profile.

Approval preparation and commit bind the normalized tool, parameters, tenant, principal, destination, data scope, expiry, idempotency identity, and action revision; mutation, replay, competing decisions, and required-audit failure refuse publication.

Arbitrary/model-generated command execution is disabled and local fallback is refused, reducing the first-profile attack surface. The non-conditional gate still lacks exact-cluster adversarial escape, path, process-flood, DNS/loopback/metadata, and credential-discovery results for the runtime boundary.

Every admitted tool carries and validates the complete production policy contract.
